raw_response:
I am 59 this year, and I have farmed here in Quzhou for many years, so I still mostly judge by what I saw on my own land and what other people around me are doing. I finished middle school, so I do listen to the township technicians, but in the end I still compare with my own fields. I have 65 mu total, not too small, not really big either, so I cannot be careless with money, but I also cannot manage it like a tiny household plot. Wheat and maize are still my backbone because that rotation is steady and I know it well. The vegetables and cash crops bring better money if the year goes smoothly, but they also need more labor and more pesticide, so I cannot put too much land into the riskiest crops. We only have 3 people in the family, so for the crops that need close watching like cabbage, chili, and watermelon, I keep the area moderate. Since I have well water, I am less afraid of dry weather, but pumping costs money, so I will not irrigate more than needed. For fertilizer, I will not cut too hard, because if wheat or maize turns yellow from lack of nitrogen, the loss is bigger than the savings.
